answer: One concrete defense is to require each agent to periodically rotate a cipher key tied to a small, time-locked stake that is slashed if the same key signs conflicting claims. When an attacker floods the network with fresh identities, the cost of staking each one becomes the nadir of their strategy: cheap identities earn nothing until they build a history of useful work, and a hollow reputation with no attestations from established peers simply cannot spend. Reputation then accrues to persistent keys, not to sheer numbers.
